draft.title: Urbanisation in Indonesia
card: Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia, on the island of Java. It grew fast as many people moved from rural areas to find work.
This rapid growth put heavy pressure on the city. Jakarta has bad flooding and heavy traffic.
Many people and businesses pump water out of the ground. As the water is removed, the land can slowly sink. Parts of Jakarta are sinking, which makes flooding worse.
These problems led Indonesia to build a new capital called Nusantara on the island of Borneo. The plan is to move government there and ease the pressure on Jakarta.
draft.remember: Jakarta's fast growth brought flooding, traffic and sinking land, so Indonesia is building a new capital, Nusantara.

a.q: Why is some of Jakarta sinking?
opts: Groundwater is pumped out from under the city
Rivers have worn away the soil beneath the city
Heavy traffic has pressed down on the roads
Farmland around the city has been built over
a.why: When people and businesses pump water out of the ground, the land above can slowly sink. Traffic is a problem in Jakarta, but the card links the sinking to groundwater pumping.
a.clue: Think about what is being taken out from under the ground.

b.q: Which statement best explains why Indonesia is building Nusantara on Borneo?
opts: Jakarta's fast growth caused flooding and traffic problems
Jakarta has lost most of its people to rural areas
Borneo has more people than any other Indonesian island
Jakarta no longer has any jobs or services to offer
b.why: Jakarta grew fast and now faces flooding, traffic and sinking land, so a new capital is planned to ease the pressure. Jakarta did not lose its people: it grew as people moved in.
b.clue: Think about what rapid growth did to Jakarta.
